tagline: Gravel connects pinyon woodland with the hollowed cliffs of Hole-in-the-Wall.
intro: Wild Horse Canyon Scenic Backcountry Byway runs through the center of Mojave National Preserve on gravel, passing near Wild Horse Mesa and the volcanic formations of Hole-in-the-Wall. The Federal Highway Administration identifies it as a National Park Service Backcountry Byway and highlights those formations along its 12 miles. NPS lists Wildhorse Canyon as four-wheel-drive only, with sand, rocks and uneven breaks in some sections.

At the northern end, the woodland bears evidence of a more recent change: the Hackberry Fire swept through in June 2005. Its effects remain visible at Mid Hills, although pinyon pine and juniper survive in the back half of the campground.

Start at the Mid Hills end, where the campground lies about two miles west of Black Canyon Road. Follow Wild Horse Canyon Road toward its southern junction with Black Canyon Road; Hole-in-the-Wall lies just north of that junction. There, rhyolite cliffs are riddled with holes and hollows.

moments.title: Mid Hills
moments.text: Pinyon pine and juniper give Mid Hills its woodland character. This low mountain range lies entirely within Mojave National Preserve. At the campground, the effects of the June 2005 Hackberry Fire remain evident. The back half retains stands of pinyon pine and juniper that shade campsites. The campground sits at the northern end of Wild Horse Canyon Road, about two miles west of Black Canyon Road.

moments.title: Mid Hills to Hole-in-the-Wall Trail
moments.text: An eight-mile, one-way hike links the Mid Hills and Hole-in-the-Wall ends of this landscape. The trail passes through washes with barrel and cholla cacti and through ground burned by the Hackberry Fire. Its total elevation gain is 1,200 feet. One trailhead is at the Mid Hills Campground entrance; the southern trailhead is about a mile west of Black Canyon Road on Wild Horse Canyon Road.

moments.title: Hole-in-the-Wall
moments.text: Holes and hollows perforate the rhyolite cliffs at Hole-in-the-Wall, just north of Wild Horse Canyon Road’s southern junction with Black Canyon Road. These volcanic formations are among the features the Federal Highway Administration highlights along the byway. The visitor center is the gateway to the Rings Trail, which runs through Banshee Canyon. NPS identifies Hole-in-the-Wall’s information center as the preserve’s primary visitor stop.
moments.notice: Holes and hollows mark the rhyolite cliffs.

practical: Mid Hills: Wildhorse Canyon is listed as four-wheel-drive only. NPS does not recommend Mid Hills Campground for RVs. UTVs and ATVs are prohibited on all preserve roads. (checked 2026-10-11)
